registered_before: any number of burden-reduction-v1 (no window table, burden or campaign metric of any lever exists yet)
change: adds two evidence-discounting levers from the literature; nothing of v1 is changed or dropped

levers.L5_peer_seen: ReplicaWatcher (El Khairi et al., NDSS 2024): replicas of one workload run the same code, so behaviour also seen on a peer replica is likely benign (exec probes, config or traffic shifts), while an attack hits one replica. Per window: novel_peer_T = number of syscall IDs in the window's context (current + 3 previous windows of the container) that no OTHER replica of the same workload showed in the last T seconds, T in {30, 60}. A window with novel_peer_T = 0 carries no evidence (CUSUM increment 0, k-of-n window not passed). A workload without another replica in the last T seconds is never discounted.
levers.L6_self_recurrent: NoDoze (Hassan et al., NDSS 2019): behaviour that recurs in the host's own history is likely benign. Per window: novel_self_T = number of syscall IDs in the context that the same container did not show in its own windows from T seconds ago up to the start of the context, T in {60, 300}. A window with novel_self_T = 0 carries no evidence. A container with less than T seconds of history is never discounted.
levers.applies_to: every L1, L2 and L3 rule

simpler_order: L1 < L2 < L3 < L5 < L6 < combinations (used only for ties within 5 %)
stated_in_advance: L5 and L6 look only at which syscall IDs appear, not their counts: an attack made only of syscalls the container or its peers use anyway (count-only anomaly) loses evidence; recall is checked per scenario
an attacker who repeats an action on the same container is discounted by L6 after the first time (the first alarm opens an incident)
the campaign attacks run on one replica, which favours L5; a simultaneous attack on all replicas would not be caught by L5 (stated by ReplicaWatcher too)

considered_not_registered.BH on conformal p-values across containe: under the global null it reduces to a stricter per-window threshold, which the alpha and CUSUM grids already span
considered_not_registered.online FDR (LORD, SAFFRON, ADDIS; Kroene: thresholds shrink while no discovery is made (alpha-death), unsuited to a 24/7 monitor without resets
considered_not_registered.other stopping rules: CUSUM is minimax-optimal for delay vs false-alarm run length given the per-window evidence (Lorden 1971, Moustakides 1986), so gains must come from better evidence (L3, L5, L6), not another stopping rule
considered_not_registered.command-line / provenance triage (NoDoze: acts after the ML preview on RCA context; left to the owner's decision on the alert pipeline
